Problem Statement
Design an interface Billable with three abstract methods — units(), unitRate() and fixedCharge() — and three default methods:
energyCharge() returning units × unit rate.
totalBill() returning energy charge + fixed charge.
printBill() printing the three output lines.
Three classes implement Billable:
DomesticConnection — rate Rs. 5.00 per unit, fixed charge Rs. 50.00.
CommercialConnection — rate Rs. 8.00 per unit, fixed charge Rs. 150.00.
IndustrialConnection — rate Rs. 6.00 per unit, fixed charge Rs. 500.00.

A single line with two tokens separated by a space.

Token 2: the units consumed, a real number.
Output Format

Line 2: Fixed Charge = <value>
Line 3: Total Bill = <value>
All values printed with exactly two decimal places.
Constraints
0.0 ≤ units ≤ 100000.0
Every method that implements an interface method must be declared public.
The fixed charge is applied once, whatever the number of units — even when the units are zero.
Test Cases
Input
	Expected Output
	
DOMESTIC 150
	Energy Charge = 750.00
Fixed Charge = 50.00
Total Bill = 800.00
	
COMMERCIAL 200
	Energy Charge = 1600.00
Fixed Charge = 150.00
Total Bill = 1750.00

assignment_context:
Assignment Title: Electricity Bill by Connection Type

Assignment Question:
Problem Statement
Design an interface Billable with three abstract methods — units(), unitRate() and fixedCharge() — and three default methods:
energyCharge() returning units × unit rate.
totalBill() returning energy charge + fixed charge.
printBill() printing the three output lines.
Three classes implement Billable:
DomesticConnection — rate Rs. 5.00 per unit, fixed charge Rs. 50.00.
CommercialConnection — rate Rs. 8.00 per unit, fixed charge Rs. 150.00.
IndustrialConnection — rate Rs. 6.00 per unit, fixed charge Rs. 500.00.
Read the connection type and the units consumed, then print the bill. There are no slabs in this problem — one flat rate applies to every unit.
Input Format
A single line with two tokens separated by a space.
Token 1: the connection type, exactly one of DOMESTIC, COMMERCIAL or INDUSTRIAL.
Token 2: the units consumed, a real number.
Output Format
Line 1: Energy Charge = <value>
Line 2: Fixed Charge = <value>
Line 3: Total Bill = <value>
All values printed with exactly two decimal places.
Constraints
0.0 ≤ units ≤ 100000.0
Every method that implements an interface method must be declared public.
The fixed charge is applied once, whatever the number of units — even when the units are zero.
Test Cases
Input
	Expected Output
	
DOMESTIC 150
	Energy Charge = 750.00
Fixed Charge = 50.00
Total Bill = 800.00
	
COMMERCIAL 200
	Energy Charge = 1600.00
Fixed Charge = 150.00
Total Bill = 1750.00
